name: Component Diagram
description: Component Diagram describes independent software components, their provided/required interfaces, and dependencies between components. This diagram is commonly used at the application architecture or module level.
purpose: Design microservices architecture, monolith modules, or declare dependencies with third-party systems.
bestFor: Describe modules in a large monolith
Declare dependencies with third-party systems or shared libraries
Create architecture documentation defining component responsibilities and boundaries
notSuitableFor: Describe server/deployment node → use Deployment Diagram
Describe detailed classes inside component → use Class Diagram
Describe API call flow in order → use Sequence Diagram
useCases: Identify provided interfaces (API the component provides)
Identify required interfaces (API the component needs to operate)
Add ports if needed (REST, AMQP, gRPC)
requirements: Provided Interfaces — API the service provides
Required Interfaces — API/library the component needs

elements.name: Required Interface
elements.description: API/library the component needs to operate

elements.name: Port
elements.description: Communication point on the component boundary

confusableWith.difference: Component describes software structure; Deployment describes what infrastructure the software is deployed on.
Component at runtime/deployable module level; Package at source code organization level.
Component Diagram does not go into details of class attributes/methods.
